kind: read-only source audit and concrete migration recommendation; not implementation acceptance
head: 7043494b394a4f57c9ddf272e67aed2984ba57a9
facts: Existing envelope writer uses independent256bit DEK for every secret, raw24byte XChaCha nonce for payload and wrap,48byte wrappedDEK, shared row KEK version1.
PgMailStore separately persists SMTP and IMAP wraps. All nonce/wrap columns are unrestricted BYTEA. One key_version serves both fields; SMTP update changes it, IMAP update does not.
Configure owner encrypts supplied passwords only; send/sync owners decrypt through same application-owned port. Existing AAD encodes exact org/account/field as length-prefixed bytes.
aws-lc-rs1.18.1 is already workspace-pinned with non-fips feature. Its AES_256_GCM is256bit key/96bit nonce/128bit tag. RandomizedNonceKey supports this algorithm and produces nonces internally.

recommendation.key: Retain master key env and KEK version1; no key rotation or historical reseal. Do not use shared key_version to identify algorithm.
recommendation.new_field_format: Both nonces exactly12bytes; dek_wrapped exactly49bytes consisting of byte0x02 followed by48byte AES256GCM ciphertext+tag of32byteDEK. Secret ciphertext contains16byteGCMtag.
recommendation.legacy_field_format: Both nonces exactly24bytes; dek_wrapped exactly48bytes. Frozen legacy XChaCha read and original AAD remain unchanged.
recommendation.dispatch: Exact format tuple selects one algorithm. Reject unknown marker, wrong lengths, mixed format and unsupported key version; never attempt fallback after authentication failure.
recommendation.new_aad: Bind constant v2 algorithm/domain, exact existing Aad.encode() and distinct payload/wrap purpose to each AES authentication. Do not modify the legacy AAD codec.
recommendation.implementation: Use existing aws_lc_rs::aead::RandomizedNonceKey with AES_256_GCM and seal_in_place_append_tag/open_in_place. Generate DEK with existing provider rand::fill. No custom AES/GHASH/nonce-generator. Keep public application port/value shape unchanged; update explanatory docs.
recommendation.secret_lifetime: Zeroizing guards own DEK, plaintext seal buffer and in-place open buffer before fallible operations. Transfer successful plaintext only into SecretBox. No cleartext in logs/errors.
recommendation.nonce_budget: Document aggregate per-KEK lifetime randomized96bit wrapping invocation budget across processes/replicas (at most2^32); key rotation support is existing separate unfinished work, not delivered by format migration.

rollout_and_rollback: New reader can read exact old and new field bundles, including mixed SMTP/IMAP formats under same KEK version. Old reader cannot read new format.

Before exposure, all potential readers including send/sync workers and rollback artifact must support both formats. Drain old consumers before enabling new writes; no mixed old-reader/new-writer rollout. This implementation task does not deploy or rotate production.

Rollback after any AES write requires an AES-aware previous artifact; do not promise rollback to XChaCha-only binary or bulk decrypt/reseal. Existing ciphertext/keys retained without database migration.
acceptance: Review exact successor to existing nonce-length assertions; preserve all existing tamper,AAD,wrongkey/version,empty/redaction checks.
Frozen original pre-change SMTP and IMAP vectors decrypt byte-exactly without mutation; independent fixture bytes, not newwriter-produced legacy fixtures.
AES256GCM known-answer authentication/open through production primitive, plus normal new envelope roundtrip and fresh nonce/DEK checks.
Reject every mixed/unknown format, modified version marker, truncation/tag/nonce/wrap/AAD corruption with no plaintext.
Real PgMailStore insert/read/reopen of historical bundle then SMTP-only and IMAP-only password updates, byte-exact preservation of untouched field, shared key_version unchanged.
Buck2 cipher/application/affected adapter checks with discovered/executed counts. Existing four SQLx mail_account RLS fixture uses SET ROLE, so actual LOGIN qualification must be labeled separately.
limitations: Algorithm choice is AES256GCM; no FIPS module certification or production qualification claim.
No production credentials inspected, no crypto rotation, no historical migration changes.
